claim: Bailey, Borwein, Lopez de Prado & Zhu state hold-out is unreliable for investment backtests and propose PBO estimated via CSCV (J. Computational Finance abstract).
quote: Standard statistical techniques designed to prevent regression overfitting, such as hold-out, tend to be unreliable and inaccurate in the context of investment backtests.
title: The Probability of Backtest Overfitting

claim: Lopez de Prado (2018), as summarized by CXO Advisory: simple walk-forward uses a single train and single test subsample, and is susceptible to overfitting.
quote: Simple walk-forward testing specifies a single training subsample that may be unrepresentative and a single test subsample that may be unrepresentative, and is susceptible to overfitting.
title: CXO Advisory summary of Lopez de Prado '10 Reasons' (secondary)

claim: DSR inputs per the same summary: return mean/stdev, non-normality, sample length, number of independent trials, data snooping; apply after counting walk-forward trials.
quote: DSR considers non-normality of returns, length of the training sample, number of independent trials and intensity of
title: CXO Advisory summary (secondary)

claim: Lopez de Prado claim: 20 repeated walk-forward backtests on the same data likely yield one useless strategy at naive 95% confidence.
quote: Just 20 walk-forward (“out-of-sample”) backtests repeated on the same data are likely to generate one useless investment strategy that has a naive 95%  confidence level .
title: CXO Advisory summary (secondary)

claim: quantstrat implements the Deflated Sharpe Ratio with p-value from observed Sharpe, number of trials and portfolio moments, citing Bailey and Lopez de Prado (2014).
quote: Per Bailey and Lopex de Prado (2014), construct a Deflated Sharpe Ratio and associated p-value based on an observed Sharpe ratio and information drawn
title: quantstrat deflatedSharpe docs

claim: Tastylive (vendor) states it closes winners at 50% profit, lower for calendars, diagonals, iron flies.
quote: We tend to close our winners when we reach 50% profit, or lower for certain strategies like calendar spreads , diagonal spreads and iron flies .
title: Managing Winning Options Positions (tastylive)

claim: Tastylive (vendor) calls 50% the 'sweet spot over the long run for most trades', a risk/reward rationale, no figures on the page.
quote: We’ve found that the target of managing our winning trades at 50% can be the sweet spot over the long run for most trades.
title: Managing Winning Options Positions (tastylive)

claim: Early assignment of a short call is more likely when the same-strike put's extrinsic value is below the upcoming dividend (put-call parity). Read via search summary only; Schwab page cache was thin.
quote: if a trader is short an ITM call and the extrinsic value of the corresponding put is less than the upcoming dividend, the trader is more likely to be subject to early assignment
title: Understanding Dividend Risk (Schwab)

claim: Forum rule of thumb: about 30 trades minimum; a few hundred preferred. Not a validated threshold; read via search summary.
quote: Minimum number of trades required for backtesting results to be trusted
title: EliteTrader thread (forum)

claim: Early exercise of a call before ex-date makes economic sense only when the remaining time value is less than the dividend.
quote: Time value must be less than the dividend for early exercise to make economic sense. Exercising forfeits remaining time value, so the dividend needs to exceed that amount.
title: Dividends and Their Effect on Options (Series 7 study material)
note: added by orchestrator; exam-prep source, textbook-level rule

claim: Open interest is not updated intraday; OCC posts it the morning after the session.
quote: open interest is a lagging number: it’s not updated during the course of a trading day. Instead, it is officially posted by The OCC the morning after any given trading session
title: Keeping Tabs on Open Interest
